title: AdvBench Construction and GCG Evaluation Workflow

nodes.label:
Define the Guardrail-Bypass Threat Model
Test Whether Aligned Models Can Be Induced
to Produce Content They Normally Refuse

Curate 500 Harmful Strings
Toxic, Threatening, Misleading, Discriminatory,
Cybercrime, Dangerous, or Illegal Content
3-44 LLaMA Tokens • Mean 16

Curate 500 Harmful Behaviors
Formulate the Same Broad Themes as Instructions
Success Means an Attempt to Comply, Not Refusal

Define the Optimization Target
String: Exact Target Continuation
Behavior: Affirmative Prefix Consistent with Compliance

Initialize a 20-Token Adversarial Suffix
Attach It to One or Multiple Prompts
Aggregate Losses across Prompts and Models

Run Greedy Coordinate Gradient Search
Gradient Top-k 256 • Candidate Batch 512
Replace One Token with the Lowest-Loss Candidate

Select the Attack Protocol
Individual: First 100 Items, One Model
Universal: 25 Train + 100 Held-Out Behaviors
Transfer: 25 Behaviors across 2 or 4 Source Models

Keep the Best Suffix after 500 Steps
Run Victim Models with Their Default Chat Templates
Evaluate White-Box and Black-Box Transfer

Harmful-String Scoring
Exact Target String Appears = Success
Also Record Target Cross-Entropy Loss

Harmful-Behavior Scoring
Judge a Reasonable Attempt to Execute the Instruction
Human Review May Separate Compliance from Refusal

Compute Attack Success Rate
Individual ASR • Universal Train/Test ASR
Transfer ASR on 388 Test Behaviors

Compare Attack Methods and Transfer
PEZ • GBDA • AutoPrompt • GCG
Source Models → Open and Proprietary Targets

Report Robustness and Universality
Higher ASR Means More Successful Guardrail Bypass
Lower Target Loss Is Better for String Elicitation
